Audit /home/user/ndarray's 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) substrate for an architecture review. Report only what exists with exact file:line citations. Never invent. Distinguish MEASURED (actual benchmark/test output) from CLAIMED (doc-comment prose, plan-doc aspiration).

Context: a prior audit pass checked only /home/user/lance-graph for "surfel"/"splat address"/hexagonal-adjacency and found nothing real (only a metaphorical CAM-plane splat in lance-graph-contract). It did NOT check ndarray, which turns out to have a substantial real 3DGS effort: `src/hpc/splat3d/` (with `gaussian.rs`), `benches/splat3d_bench.rs`, `tests/splat3d_correctness.rs`, `examples/splat3d_flex.rs`, and TEN+ planning docs under `.claude/plans/3DGS-*.md` (3DGS-4x4-cognitive-shader-SoA-plan.md, 3DGS-certified-field-kernel-substrate-plan.md, 3DGS-EWA-SYRK-BLAS-MKL-crosspollination-plan.md, 3DGS-error-certification-pillars-plan.md, 3DGS-render-depth-certification-plan.md, 3DGS-HHTL-CPU-cascade-plan.md, 3DGS-SIMD-forward-renderer-plan.md, 3DGS-validation-benchmark-plan.md, 3DGS-columnar-splat-codec-plan.md, 3DGS-PLAN-INDEX.md) plus a knowledge doc `pr-x12-x266-3dgs-spacetime-upscaling.md`.

Tasks:
1. Read `src/hpc/splat3d/gaussian.rs` in full. What is the actual Gaussian/splat type — does it carry a real "surfel"-like address (position + covariance + opacity + spatial index)? Is there a literal "surfel" struct anywhere in this module (grep -i "surfel" across all of src/hpc/splat3d/)? What is the actual memory layout (bytes per splat)?
2. Read `.claude/plans/3DGS-PLAN-INDEX.md` in full — it should summarize the other plan docs' status (built/planned/proposed). Report each plan's stated status verbatim.
3. Read `.claude/plans/3DGS-HHTL-CPU-cascade-plan.md` in full — this is the most relevant to a "HHTL + spatial splat + cascade" hypothesis. Is this BUILT (cite the actual code it produced) or still a PROPOSAL? Quote its own status line.
4. Read `.claude/plans/3DGS-4x4-cognitive-shader-SoA-plan.md` in full — does this describe wiring the splat substrate into the cognitive-shader/SoA machinery (relevant cross-repo, since cognitive-shader-driver lives in lance-graph)? Built or proposed? Quote status.
5. Read `benches/splat3d_bench.rs` and `tests/splat3d_correctness.rs` in full or as much as needed. Extract ANY real measured timing numbers (criterion output format, ns/µs/ms). Quote exactly, with what operation was measured (e.g. "one splat rasterization pass over N splats"). Also report test count and what correctness properties are actually verified (radiometric/geometric fidelity? just "doesn't panic"?).
6. Does this splat3d module implement anything resembling a fixed spatial ADJACENCY scheme — is a splat addressed/indexed by a tile/grid position with neighbor relationships (even approximately, e.g. a screen-space tile binning scheme, which real 3DGS rasterizers use)? Cite exact structure. This is relevant to whether ndarray's splat3d could serve as the "spatial BLASGraph ALU" substrate a hypothesis proposes.
7. Is splat3d wired to or referenced FROM lance-graph anywhere (check crates/jc/src/ewa_sandwich_3d.rs in lance-graph, which a prior audit found references "ndarray::hpc::splat3d")? Confirm that cross-repo reference is real — does lance-graph actually import/depend on ndarray's splat3d, or is it just named in a comment?

Output: structured report per question, exact citations, exact quoted numbers with provenance (bench output vs. prose). This is significant new territory a prior audit pass entirely missed — be thorough.

12	HEEL  coarse tile/block rejection

15	LEAF  exact projection/render payload

1	# 3DGS 4x4 Cognitive-Shader SoA Plan — ndarray
2	
3	## Goal
4	
5	Promote the 3DGS math carrier from a narrow 3x3-only view into a 4x4 cognitive-shader-friendly SoA carrier while preserving the correct 3DGS covariance spine.
6	
7	Important distinction:
8	
9	```text
10	3x3 SPD covariance
11	  remains the mathematically correct spatial covariance for each 3D Gaussian
12	
13	4x4 carrier
14	  becomes the homogeneous / temporal / semantic / shader-lane envelope around that covariance
15	```
16	
17	Do not destroy the 3x3 SPD invariant. Lift it into a 4x4 block where needed.
18	
19	## Why 4x4
20	
21	The 4x4 shape maps better to:
22	
23	```text
24	homogeneous transforms
25	SIMD lane groups
26	cognitive-shader-driver BindSpace columns
27	Mat4 camera/world transforms
28	quaternion / covariance / opacity packing
29	(4x4)^4 tensor-block fanout
30	```
31	
32	It also gives a natural bridge between rendering, registration, ultrasound frame fusion, genetics-like transition matrices, and neuronal adjacency blocks.
33	
34	## Core representation
35	
36	Add or stabilize a Mat4 carrier under the existing linalg path:
37	
38	```text
39	src/hpc/linalg/
40	  mat4.rs
41	  spd4.rs
42	  block4.rs
43	```
44	
45	Candidate types:
46	
47	```rust
48	pub struct Mat4x4<T> {
49	    pub m: [[T; 4]; 4],
50	}
51	
52	pub struct Sym4<T> {
53	    pub a00: T, pub a01: T, pub a02: T, pub a03: T,
54	                pub a11: T, pub a12: T, pub a13: T,
55	                            pub a22: T, pub a23: T,
56	                                        pub a33: T,
57	}
58	
59	pub struct Splat4Carrier<T> {
60	    pub spatial_sigma_3x3: [T; 6],
61	    pub lane4: [T; 4],
62	    pub transform4x4: Mat4x4<T>,
63	}
64	```
65	
66	## 3x3 to 4x4 lift
67	
68	Use explicit lifts instead of pretending 3x3 and 4x4 mean the same thing.
69	
70	```text
71	3DGS spatial covariance Sigma3
72	        ->
73	4x4 homogeneous carrier Sigma4
74	        ->
75	projection / temporal / semantic / shader lane operations
76	        ->
77	extract spatial 3x3 or image-space 2x2 when needed
78	```
79	
80	Example lift:
81	
82	```rust
83	pub fn lift_spd3_to_sym4(sigma3: [f32; 6], w_lane: [f32; 4]) -> Sym4<f32>;
84	pub fn extract_spd3_from_sym4(sym4: Sym4<f32>) -> [f32; 6];
85	```
86	
87	## Cognitive-shader SoA layout
88	
89	Prefer 4-lane grouped SoA columns:
90	
91	```text
92	BindSpace4
93	  lane0: position / nucleotide / neuron source / feature id shard
94	  lane1: covariance / transition / edge weight / local statistic
95	  lane2: opacity / expression / activation / confidence
96	  lane3: time / phase / semantic role / provenance
97	```
98	
99	Concrete splat columns:
100	
101	```text
102	pos_xyzw[]
103	scale_xyz_opacity[]
104	quat_xyzw[]
105	color_rgba[]
106	feature_id_time[]
107	certificate_confidence[]
108	```
109	
110	## (4x4)^4 tensor-block fanout
111	
112	Interpret `(4x4)^4` as a four-level block grammar, not as one giant dense matrix.
113	
114	```text
115	level 0: Mat4 local carrier
116	level 1: 4x4 block of carriers
117	level 2: 4x4 block of blocks
118	level 3: 4x4 graph/tile/neural field super-block
119	```
120	
121	This gives hierarchical locality:
122	
123	```text
124	splat -> block -> tile -> region -> graph domain
125	```
126	
127	## Domain-neutral kernels
128	
129	Create kernels that do not care whether the 4x4 block is geospatial, ultrasound, genetic, or neuronal.
130	
131	```rust
132	pub trait Block4Kernel<T> {
133	    fn score_block(&self, block: &Block4<T>) -> f32;
134	    fn contract(&self, parent: &Block4<T>, child: &Block4<T>) -> f32;

139	## 3DGS compatibility rules
140	
141	- Keep `Spd3` as the authoritative spatial covariance.
142	- Use `Mat4x4` for transforms and carriers.
143	- Use `Sym4` only when the extra lane has defined meaning.
144	- Image-space EWA still extracts the proper spatial covariance path.
145	- Pillar tests must assert that 4x4 lifts do not break 3x3 invariants.

1	//! CPU-SIMD 3D Gaussian Splatting forward renderer (Kerbl et al. 2023).
2	//!
3	//! # Mission
4	//!
5	//! Render anisotropic 3D gaussians to a 2D image plane via the
6	//! Elliptical-Weighted-Average (EWA) splatting pipeline of Zwicker 2001 /
7	//! Kerbl 2023. All on the CPU, all in SIMD, no GPU, no wgpu, no new
8	//! top-level dependencies. Target: ≥30 fps at 1080p with 500K gaussians
9	//! on an 8-core AVX-512 box; NEON and AVX2 paths as graceful fallbacks.
10	//!
11	//! # The pipeline (forward pass)
12	//!
13	//! ```text
14	//!  GaussianBatch                Camera
15	//!  (μ, scale, quat, opacity,    (V, K, near/far,
16	//!   SH coefficients)             image dims)
17	//!         │                          │
18	//!         └───────────┬──────────────┘
19	//!                     ▼
20	//!              project_batch  ── J·W·Σ·Wᵀ·Jᵀ (EWA-sandwich, Pillar 7)
21	//!                     │           depth + 2D conic + 3σ radius + SH→RGB
22	//!                     ▼
23	//!              ProjectedBatch (SoA)
24	//!                     │
25	//!                     ▼
26	//!              TileBinning   ── 16×16 tile grid, AABB intersection,
27	//!                     │         radix-sort (tile_id, depth)
28	//!                     ▼
29	//!              raster_frame  ── per-tile alpha-blend front-to-back,
30	//!                     │         F32x16-wide pixels per inner loop
31	//!                     ▼
32	//!              framebuffer: Vec<f32>  (RGB, length = 3 · W · H)
33	//! ```
34	//!
35	//! # Architectural invariants — DO NOT VIOLATE
36	//!
37	//! 1. **Zero-dep on hot path.** No `serde`, no `tokio`, no `glam`. Use
38	//!    `crate::simd::{F32x16, PREFERRED_F32_LANES}` for all SIMD.
39	//! 2. **SoA, 64-byte aligned, padded to `PREFERRED_F32_LANES`.** Every
40	//!    buffer length is `pad_to_lanes(n, L)`. No scalar tails.
41	//! 3. **Click P-1 method discipline.** Operations on carriers:
42	//!    `frame.bin_tile(g)`, not `bin_tile(frame, g)`.
43	//! 4. **`#[repr(C, align(N))]` on cross-FFI structs, `#[repr(u8)]` on
44	//!    enums.** No `#[derive(Serialize)]`.
45	//! 5. **Per-tier SIMD via `crate::simd` polyfill.** Same pattern as
46	//!    `hpc::vsa`. Compile-time routes to AVX-512 / AVX2 / NEON /
47	//!    scalar — never hand-write intrinsics here.
48	//! 6. **Module docs lead with the math.** Every `.rs` opens with `//!`
49	//!    stating the equation it implements and citing the paper section.
50	//! 7. **The cognitive `splat.rs` is sacred.** `lance_graph_contract::splat`
51	//!    is the cognitive splat (CAM-plane deposition); this `splat3d` is
52	//!    the graphics splat. They are siblings, not parent/child.
53	//!
54	//! # Module layout (PRs landing in order)
55	//!
56	//! - [`spd3`] — symmetric 3×3 SPD math: Smith-1961 eigendecomp,
57	//!   `Spd3::pow(t)`, `sqrt`, `log_spd`, `from_scale_quat`,
58	//!   `sandwich(M, N)` + `sandwich_x16`. **PR 1.**
59	//! - [`gaussian`] — `GaussianBatch` SoA storage + `Gaussian3D`
60	//!   convenience constructor. **PR 2.**
61	//! - [`sh`] — degree-3 spherical-harmonics evaluator (RGB color
62	//!   from view direction). **PR 2.**
63	//! - `project` — EWA projection kernel. **PR 3.**
64	//! - `tile` — frustum cull + tile binning + radix sort. **PR 4.**
65	//! - `raster` — depth-sorted alpha-blend with `F32x16` pixel rows. **PR 5.**
66	//! - `frame` — `SplatFrame` double-buffer (sibling of
67	//!   `hpc::renderer::RenderFrame`). **PR 6.**
68	//!
69	//! # SIMD dispatch
70	//!
71	//! All SIMD goes through `crate::simd::F32x16`. The polyfill picks the
72	//! native width at compile time: AVX-512 (1× __m512), AVX2 (2× __m256),
73	//! NEON (4× float32x4_t), or scalar `[f32; 16]`. Consumer code never
74	//! mentions the tier — write once, run everywhere the workspace builds.
75	//!
76	//! ```ignore
77	//! use ndarray::simd::F32x16;
78	//!
79	//! let a = F32x16::splat(2.0);
80	//! let b = F32x16::from_slice(&[1.0; 16]);
81	//! let c = a.mul_add(b, F32x16::splat(0.5));  // a*b + 0.5, lanewise

5	//!
6	//! ```text
7	//!   HEEL  reject blocks behind near/far or outside the frustum
8	//!   HIP   screen-space error (Cesium SSE) + projected screen radius → priority
9	//!   TWIG  depth certificate → ordering / occlusion / depth-error refinement
10	//!   LEAF  exact-projection / render action
11	//! ```
12	//!
13	//! # Cesium reverse-engineered with our advantages
14	//!
15	//! Vanilla Cesium accepts a tile when `sse ≤ maximumScreenSpaceError`. We keep
16	//! that test (HIP) but gate acceptance on the **depth certificate** (TWIG): a
17	//! block is only kept coarse when its SSE is small *and* its depth interval is
18	//! within budget *and* its occlusion confidence clears the threshold. The
19	//! certificate adds depth/ordering/occlusion uncertainty that flat SSE can't
20	//! express, so refinement decisions are auditable rather than a single scalar.
21	//!
22	//! All math goes through `crate::simd::F32x16` (HEEL batch reject) or the
23	//! scalar reference; no SIMD-dispatch code lives here.

30	/// sphere variant of Cesium's `boundingVolume`, matching `cesium::hlod`'s
31	/// `distance_to_camera`).

33	#[repr(C)]
34	pub struct BlockBounds {
35	    /// World-space sphere centre.
36	    pub center: [f32; 3],

43	#[repr(u8)]

46	    Hip = 1,
47	    Twig = 2,

58	    KeepCoarse = 1,

96	    pub action: HhtlAction,
97	    /// Screen-space error (px) — Cesium priority; higher ⇒ more refinement.
98	    pub priority: f32,
99	    /// Estimated screen error (px) used for the LOD decision (= SSE here).
100	    pub estimated_error_px: f32,
101	    /// Projected screen radius (px).
102	    pub projected_radius_px: f32,
103	    /// The render-depth certificate produced at TWIG (zeroed if rejected at HEEL).
104	    pub certificate: RenderDepthCertificate,
105	}

107	/// Transform a world point by the upper 3 rows of the row-major view matrix.
108	#[inline]
109	fn to_camera(view: &[[f32; 4]; 4], p: [f32; 3]) -> [f32; 3] {
110	    let row = |r: usize| view[r][0] * p[0] + view[r][1] * p[1] + view[r][2] * p[2] + view[r][3];
111	    [row(0), row(1), row(2)]
112	}
113	
114	/// HEEL broad-phase reject (scalar reference): `true` ⇒ drop the block.
115	///
116	/// Rejects blocks entirely behind the near plane, entirely beyond the far
117	/// plane, or whose projected screen AABB is fully off-screen (same cull logic
118	/// as `project::project_chunk_x16`, at block granularity).
119	pub fn heel_reject_scalar(camera: &Camera, block: &BlockBounds) -> bool {
120	    let c = to_camera(&camera.view, block.center);
121	    let (cam_x, cam_y, cam_z) = (c[0], c[1], c[2]);
122	    let r = block.radius;
123	    if cam_z + r < camera.near || cam_z - r > camera.far {
124	        return true;
125	    }
126	    // Project centre; world radius → screen px via fy / depth.
127	    let z = cam_z.max(1e-6);
128	    let projr = r * camera.fy / z;
129	    let sx = camera.fx * cam_x / z + camera.cx;
130	    let sy = camera.fy * cam_y / z + camera.cy;
131	    let w = camera.width as f32;
132	    let h = camera.height as f32;
133	    sx + projr < 0.0 || sx - projr >= w || sy + projr < 0.0 || sy - projr >= h
134	}

146	            priority: 0.0,
147	            estimated_error_px: 0.0,
148	            projected_radius_px: 0.0,
149	            certificate: RenderDepthCertificate::ZERO,
150	        };

## 6. Fixed spatial ADJACENCY / tile-binning scheme

**Yes — a real screen-space tile binning scheme exists**, in `src/hpc/splat3d/tile.rs` (605 lines):

- `TILE_SIZE: u32 = 16` — 16×16 pixel tiles (`tile.rs:37`).
- `TileInstance` struct, `#[repr(C, align(16))]`, exactly 16 bytes: `tile_id: u32` (linear `tile_y * tile_cols + tile_x`), `gaussian_id: u32`, `depth_bits: u32` (IEEE-754 bit pattern for sortable depth), `_pad: u32` (`tile.rs:44-58`).
- `TileBinning` struct: `tile_cols`, `tile_rows`, `instances: Vec<TileInstance>` (sorted), `tile_offsets: Vec<u32>` — a prefix-sum index giving O(1) per-tile slice access (`tile.rs:70-83`).
- Algorithm (`tile.rs:1-31` doc, implementation from `tile.rs:99` on): for each visible projected gaussian, compute its screen-space AABB from the 3σ bounding-circle radius, enumerate every 16×16 tile the AABB overlaps, emit one `TileInstance` per (tile, gaussian) pair, then sort by a packed `(tile_id << 32 | depth_bits)` u64 key so instances are tile-major, depth-ascending within tile (`tile.rs:12-19, 27-30`).

This is a genuine, standard 3DGS-style **screen-space grid/tile binning** scheme (each splat addressed by which grid tile(s) it touches, with depth-ordered neighbor lists per tile) — matching what real 3DGS rasterizers (the original Kerbl et al. 2023 CUDA renderer) do. It is **NOT a hexagonal-adjacency or fixed-neighbor spatial-index scheme** — no hex grid, no k-nearest-neighbor graph, no Morton/z-order code exists in `tile.rs`. It is a rectangular AABB-tile-overlap scheme, computed fresh per frame from projected screen positions, not a persistent world-space spatial index carried on the `GaussianBatch` itself. (The HHTL plan doc does mention "optional Morton range locality scan" as a HEEL primitive — `3DGS-HHTL-CPU-cascade-plan.md:27` — but that is a PROPOSAL bullet, not implemented; no Morton code exists in `tile.rs` or `depth_cascade.rs`.)

**Relevance to "spatial BLASGraph ALU" hypothesis**: this tile-binning scheme is a real, working screen-space adjacency structure, but it is 2D/per-frame/rasterization-scoped, not a persistent world-space spatial-graph/ALU substrate. Nothing in `splat3d` builds a general graph-adjacency structure over splats independent of a specific camera/frame.
